title: Effective stable versal chart with full level cover and normalized generic branches
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $g,d,\ell$ be natural numbers, and let $C$ be a stable unpointed genus-$g$ curve over $\Omega$ in the actual fibre groupoid [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Write $H=\operatorname{Aut}_\Omega(C)$, using the canonical underlying curve over its fibre base [def-sfb-stable-fiber-curve]. Define an effective stable versal level chart to consist of the following data and properties; this definition asserts neither their existence nor freeness.

Put $A=\Omega[[t_1,\ldots,t_{3g-3}]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], with affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and closed section $c:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ induced by constant coefficient, and use maximal-ideal-adic formal schemes [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. There is a bound $d\leq3g-3$, an actual stable genus-$g$ family $D$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-scheme], and a specified special-fibre isomorphism $e:D_\Omega\simeq C$. Marked formal universality means the following on every affine nilpotent thickening: for every commutative $\Omega$-algebra $R$, nilpotent ideal $I\subseteq R$, stable genus-$g$ family $X/R$, and marking $i:X_{R/I}\simeq C_{R/I}$, there is a unique pair of an $\Omega$-map $a:\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ reducing modulo $I$ to $c$, and an isomorphism $X\simeq a^*D$ whose reduction is exactly the specified marking via $e$. All maps and isomorphisms here use the actual fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. (Remark, not a condition of the chart: forgetting markings is meant to present the completion along the residual gerbe of $C$ as the formal quotient by $H$, markings being $H$-torsors with their equivariant maps; that identification is a theorem about these data and is not assumed here.) The chart carries group homomorphisms defining $H$-actions on its base and total family, compatible with the projection, fixing $c$, and restricting under $e$ to the given action on $C$.

Put $f=t_1\cdots t_d$ (empty product $1$) and $U=D(f)\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$. The smooth-family inverse image [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is exactly $U$: for every scheme $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, its pulled-back family is smooth if and only if the map factors through this open. There is a finite etale $E\to U$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and [def-weil-etale-morphism], with a tautological isomorphism from the constant rank-$2g$ module to $R^1(D_E/E)_*\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z}$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. This represents the FULL frame functor: every such frame after every base change $T\to U$ is pulled back along a unique $T\to E$, using the recorded constant-sheaf and degree-one base-change comparisons. Its $H$-action covers the one on the deformation base; its tautological frame is equivariant for the family action and the trivial action on constant labels. No symplectic condition is imposed.

Let $F=\prod_{x\in\operatorname{Gen}(E)}\kappa(x)$, the product over ALL generic points of $E$ [def-sc-generic-point], with residue fields [def-weil-residue-field], with the diagonal structural map $A\to F$ obtained by global evaluation. Put $B=\operatorname{integralClosure}_A(F)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The chart includes its canonical identification of $E$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}U$: on generic fields the map is precisely the inclusion $B\subset F$. It includes an $H$-action on $\operatorname{Spec}B$ over the one on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, extending the specified action on $E$.
